result.instructions: Tools for Asset Panda, hosted by usefulapi.io. If the user is new or asks what this server can do, suggest requests such as: "List all my asset collections and their columns."; "Which assets are assigned to the Berlin office?"; "Show the record for the laptop with serial number ABC123.". Read-only tools never change data; ask the user before a tool that creates, changes or deletes Asset Panda data. Free plan: 50 tool calls per month. Run asset_panda_usage_status to see the calls used this month. If the user asks for something none of these tools can do, tell the user and, with their OK, run asset_panda_request_feature to record the request. Paid plans: Pro (10,000 tool calls a month, $9/month or $90/year, for normal use) and Pro+ (100,000 tool calls a month, $39/month or $390/year, for automations and heavy use). A plan can be cancelled at any time and then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. When the user wants more calls or reaches the limit, run asset_panda_upgrade without a plan: it returns both plans, each with a payment link for the user to open. asset_panda_cancel_subscription cancels Pro at the end of the paid period.

tools.name: asset_panda_list_accounts
tools.title: List accounts
tools.description: List the Asset Panda accounts this API key can reach. Call this first to get an account id. API: GET /accounts.

tools.name: asset_panda_get_account
tools.title: Get account
tools.description: Get the details of one account. API: GET /account/{id}.

tools.name: asset_panda_list_modules
tools.title: List modules
tools.description: List the modules (areas such as assets or people) of an account. API: GET /modules.

tools.name: asset_panda_get_module
tools.title: Get module
tools.description: Get the details of one module. API: GET /module/{id}.

tools.name: asset_panda_list_collections
tools.title: List collections
tools.description: List the collections (groups of records, for example Assets or Locations). API: GET /collections.

tools.name: asset_panda_get_collection
tools.title: Get collection
tools.description: Get the details of one collection. API: GET /collection/{id}.

tools.name: asset_panda_list_collection_columns
tools.title: List collection columns
tools.description: List the columns (fields) of a collection with their ids and types. Use the column ids in search filters and in record writes. API: GET /collection-columns.

version.description: Column version, only if the vendor asks for it.

tools.name: asset_panda_list_categories
tools.title: List categories
tools.description: List the categories of a module. API: GET /categories.

tools.name: asset_panda_get_record
tools.title: Get record
tools.description: Get one record of a collection by its record id. API: GET /collection-record/{recordId}.

tools.name: asset_panda_search_records
tools.title: Search records
tools.description: Search the records of a collection with filters on column ids, for example assets in one location. Without filters it lists records. Read only. API: POST /collection-records/search.

match_type.description: All filters must match (default) or any filter.

value.description: Value to compare with. Not needed for isEmpty and isNotEmpty.

from.description: Zero-based index of the first record (default 0).

tools.name: asset_panda_create_records
tools.title: Create records
tools.description: WRITE: create up to 5 new records in a collection. Each record maps column ids to values. The API key needs write permission. Not safe to repeat: a second call creates duplicates. API: POST /collection-records.

items.description: Column id -> value. Get column ids from asset_panda_list_collection_columns.

tools.name: asset_panda_update_records
tools.title: Update records
tools.description: WRITE: update up to 5 existing records in a collection. Each record needs recordId plus the column ids to change. This replaces the old values of those columns. The API key needs write permission. API: PUT /collection-records.

recordId.description: Id of the record to update.

items.description: recordId plus column id -> new value for each column to change.
